misery noun

also wretchedness, distress

classical

Plaut. Truc. 4.2.31; Cic. (Lewis & Short)
Andresian p. 36
Traupman 155

miseria, miseriae f.

noun, first declension

wretchedness, misfortune

The state of the miser, often in the plural for one’s troubles.

Other words

  • aerumna, aerumnae f. — hardship, trouble

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short, s.v. aerumna

    Toil and trouble that weighs one down; an old word, frequent in comedy.

  • dolor, dolōris m. — distress, anguish

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 305

  • angustiae, angustiārum f. pl. — distress, difficulties, straits

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Quinct. 5: in summās angustiās addūcī (Lewis & Short); Traupman 305

Examples

  • nam invidēre aliī bene esse, tibi male esse, miseriast

    for to envy another his good fortune while you fare badly is miseryPlaut. Truc. 4.2.31

See also poor, sadness.
